catalysts: Evidence of stabilization or improvement in enterprise operating income as Wine & Spirits and Beer results normalize in subsequent quarters.
Progress and execution of Mexico beer capacity initiatives supporting longer-duration volume growth and margin recovery.
Sustained capital allocation (dividends and buybacks) supported by operating cash flow and free cash flow targets.
company_overview: Constellation Brands is a leading international producer and marketer of beer, wine, and spirits with operations in the U.S., Mexico, New Zealand, and Italy.
Brand portfolio is anchored by major beer brands such as Corona Extra and Modelo Especial (U.S. brand license).
Business performance is managed across Beer and Wine & Spirits segments, with corporate costs and equity-method investments in “Corporate Operations and Other.”
current_context: Q3 fiscal 2026 results: net sales of $2,223 million (reported) and reported operating income (loss) of $692 million; diluted EPS of $2.88.
Company updated fiscal 2026 outlook: reported EPS of $9.72–$10.02 and comparable EPS of $11.30–$11.60, with a reported tax rate guide of ~0.18 and operating cash flow target of $2.5–$2.6 billion.

Capex guidance for fiscal 2026 is approximately $1.2 billion (including ~$1.0 billion targeted for Mexico beer operations activities). ([d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_824e2eb8067741e0331b1bacda44d642/cbrands/db/964/9824/file/3Q26_STZ_Earnings-Release_and_Financial-Tables.pdf))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth assumes moderate re-acceleration from recent levels while reflecting ongoing category and volume volatility highlighted in management’s outlook.

Margin thesis is anchored on a normalized EBIT margin recovery toward a 0.30 target through the forecast period rather than relying on the depressed FY2025 operating income result. ([ir.cbrands.com](https://ir.cbrands.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000016918-25-000022/stz-20250228.htm))
Capital intensity is modeled using historical capex intensity (incl. Mexico beer projects) and holding capex as a % of sales near ~0.11–0.12 over the forecast period.

Tax rate is stabilized at ~0.18 per fiscal 2026 guidance to reduce earnings uncertainty versus FY2025 effective tax volatility driven by impairment-related effects. ([ir.cbrands.com](https://ir.cbrands.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000016918-25-000022/stz-20250228.htm))

Working capital needs are modeled with a gradually improving NWC intensity toward ~0.17 as the business normalizes. ([ir.cbrands.com](https://ir.cbrands.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000016918-25-000022/stz-20250228.htm))
key_risks: Downside risk from weaker-than-expected category volumes, pricing, or mix (especially in Wine & Spirits) that delays margin normalization.
Input cost and FX volatility (e.g., tariffs and commodity-driven costs) could pressure gross margin and operating leverage.

Potential for additional impairment / restructuring actions and associated tax-effect volatility (historically impacting effective tax rate). ([ir.cbrands.com](https://ir.cbrands.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000016918-25-000022/stz-20250228.htm))
Higher WACC than assumed or weaker terminal economics could materially reduce intrinsic value under the Gordon Growth terminal framework.

valuation_summary: DCF is driven by a sober two-stage operating profile: near-term growth/margin gradual improvement plus a terminal period reflecting a mature beverages business (terminal growth 0.02 with Gordon Growth).

Comps provide context that peer forward P/E ratios cluster roughly in the low teens and EV/EBITDA in a mid-single to low double-digit range, supporting a non-extreme terminal value range. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/bf.b/statistics/))

Key cash-and-debt adjustments are based on the most recent fiscal year-end balance sheet. ([ir.cbrands.com](https://ir.cbrands.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000016918-25-000022/stz-20250228.htm))
